It's beginning') do not land until after the 3-s window."},"cliffhanger":{"score":3,"reason":"The ad ends with loyalist fighters slipping inside the cathedral, leaving the rescue unresolved, but the immediate fight has already concluded and the tension has eased."},"questions":[{"q":"Are the men in the cart coming to rescue Juliana?","type":"intrigue"},{"q":"Why is Juliana imprisoned while a wedding is beginning?","type":"intrigue"},{"q":"Who is the cart driver and how does he know the loyalists?","type":"confusion"}],"standalone":{"score":3,"reason":"The dungeon and wedding bells establish that Juliana is a prisoner facing a ceremony, but the sudden shift to a cart ambush requires context to connect the attackers to her plight."},"emotion":{"score":3,"reason":"Her terror softening into a brave smile and the whispered 'Alexander...' evoke longing and defiance, but the generic fight scene dilutes the personal stakes."},"want_next":{"score":3,"reason":"The rescue attempt creates curiosity about whether Alexander's forces will reach her in time, but the disjointed pacing weakens the urgency."},"ad_policy":{"level":"mild","category":"violence","reason":"On-screen physical violence including a sentry being struck, tackled, and placed in a sleeper hold until unconscious."},"one_line_verdict":"A structurally ambitious ad with a rescue-action payoff, but undercut by a disjointed second act and a hook that needs a few extra seconds to land."},{"id":"C2","weakest_point":"The first three seconds show only a loaf of bread sliding under a door—dead calm with no conflict—and the ad ends on a resolved, tearful whisper rather than an unresolved peak.","hook":{"score":1,"reason":"Above the 3-s line there is only a guard silently passing bread through cell bars; only a prisoner receiving bread and crying."},"one_line_verdict":"An emotionally potent but dramatically inert clip that plays like a sad movie scene rather than an ad; it lacks both a scroll-stopping hook and a cliffhanger."}],"best":"C1","best_why":"C1 is the only viable ad because it pairs a dungeon premise with a late-breaking rescue action that creates forward momentum, whereas C2 is a static, tearful interlude with no hook and no cliffhanger to drive installs."}
